slides.headline: Core strength: four myths to drop
slides.sub: What clinical Pilates actually focuses on, and what it doesn't.

slides.title: Myth: a weak core causes back pain
slides.body: Research suggests the link is weaker than most people think. Plenty of people with strong abs get back pain, and plenty with average cores don't. Confidence, movement variety and overall strength often matter more.

slides.title: Myth: core means six-pack muscles
slides.body: Your core includes the deep abdominals, back muscles, diaphragm, pelvic floor and the muscles around your hips. They work together, so we train them together rather than chasing crunches.

slides.title: Myth: you must brace all day
slides.body: Constantly sucking in or bracing can make movement stiff and tiring. Most everyday tasks only need a light, automatic level of support. Save firmer bracing for heavier lifts at the gym.

slides.title: Myth: Pilates is just stretching
slides.body: Clinical Pilates is progressive strength training using mat work and equipment like the reformer. Springs add resistance or support, so sessions can be adjusted for a flare-up or built up for sport.

slides.title: Try this today: the dead bug
slides.body: Lie on your back with knees and arms up. Slowly lower the opposite arm and leg as you breathe out, keeping your lower back relaxed. Five slow reps each side is a good starting point.

slides.headline: Train your core the useful way
slides.body: Our Pilates team at Hybrid Physiotherapy starts with an assessment, then builds a program around your goals, history and how you like to move.

caption:
"Just strengthen your core" might be the most overused advice in fitness.

Your core is more than your abs. It's a team of deep abdominals, back muscles, diaphragm, pelvic floor and hip muscles, and it tends to work well when it's trained as a team. Research suggests a "weak core" isn't the simple cause of back pain it's often made out to be, and bracing all day tends to make movement stiff rather than safe.

Clinical Pilates is progressive strength training, on the mat and the reformer, that can be adjusted for a flare-up or built up for sport. Try five slow dead bugs each side today as a starting point.

story.body: A weak core isn't the simple cause of back pain, and you don't need to brace all day. Train it as a team.
